# Complex numbers

Complex numbers at two precisions: arithmetic, polar form, and the elementary functions.

<h2 id="complex"><code>Complex</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Complex {
    pub real: float64;
    pub imaginary: float64;
}
```

A complex number `real + imaginary·i` over `float64`. `Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Complex.rux#L13)

| `imaginary` | `float64` | The imaginary part. |

<h3 id="pow"><code>Pow</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Pow(self: &Complex, exponent: Complex) -> Complex
```

This number raised to `exponent`, as e raised to `exponent` times the logarithm, so on the principal branch.

| `exponent` | `Complex` | the power   |

**Returns**: the power

<h3 id="divide"><code>/</code></h3>

```rux
pub func /(self: &Complex, other: Complex) -> Complex
```

The quotient, by Smith's method, so that a divisor with very large or very small parts keeps its precision.
Dividing by zero gives infinities or NaN, as floating-point division does.

| Name    | Type      | Description             |
| ------- | --------- | ----------------------- |
| `other` | `Complex` | the number to divide by |

**Returns**: the quotient

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Complex.rux#L151)
